title: Choosing a first project
subtitle: What makes a good first crochet project and what to avoid
excerpt: A good first project uses one stitch, has no shaping, no seaming, and takes less than a week to finish. A dishcloth, a small square swatch, or a simple scarf works. A granny-square blanket or a lace shawl doesn't — not for the first project.
sourceNotes: Pauline Turner, How to Crochet — starting out advice. Edie Eckman, The Crochet Answer Book.

glossaryTerms.definition: A small sample piece, usually 15 cm x 15 cm, worked in the stitch and yarn of the project to check that gauge matches the pattern. For a beginner, the tension swatch doubles as a practice piece.
A short project that can be completed in one or two sessions, used deliberately at the start of learning to build confidence and habit before moving to longer or more complex pieces.

heroPrompt: A small finished dishcloth in cream DK cotton on a pale wooden surface — simple double crochet texture, even edges, about 20 cm x 20 cm. A 4 mm crochet hook resting beside it.

content.text: The biggest mistake a new crocheter makes is choosing an ambitious first project — a blanket, a jumper, a lace shawl — and abandoning it before finishing because it takes months and the skill level required is too far ahead of current ability. A
in the first week or two matters far more than starting something impressive.
What makes a good first project
One stitch only. Not 'mainly one stitch with a few others' — one stitch. Double crochet, or treble crochet.
No shaping. No increases, no decreases, no armhole — just rows of even stitches.
Short. A 20 x 20 cm dishcloth, not a 150 x 150 cm blanket.
DK or aran weight yarn on a 4-5 mm hook. Not lace weight, not chunky.

Plain cotton or smooth acrylic in a mid-tone colour. Avoids: white (shows dirt, hard to see stitches in), black (too dark to count stitches), fuzzy mohair (mistakes are invisible and hard to fix), and slippery silk.
The tension swatch is your first project

in double crochet: chain 21, work 20 dc across the first row and continue for 20 rows. Cast off. This 15 x 15 cm swatch is a valid tension gauge tool, a record of your starting tension, and a finished piece. Most beginners skip swatches and wish they had not. Making the swatch your actual first project removes the temptation to skip it.
Dishcloth: chain 30, dc across, 30 rows. One stitch, flat, practical, done in a sitting.
Simple scarf: chain 20, treble crochet, work until the desired length. Practises turning chains.
Flat circle: magic ring, increase to a circle in double crochet. Practises rounds, increases, counting.
